themeData.name: American Foundation
themeData.description: Johnnycakes, succotash, and election cake - these foundational recipes shaped American cuisine from colonial times through the early republic.
themeData.source: Colonial Cookbooks, Shaker Communities, Early American Archives
themeData.coverImagePrompt: Colonial American hearth kitchen with copper pots and wooden utensils, candlelit warmth, Americana folk art style

recipes.title: Colonial Brown Bread
recipes.description: One cup Indian meal, one cup rye meal, one cup graham flour, three-quarters cup molasses, two cups sour milk, two teaspoons salt, two teaspoons soda. Steam three hours.
recipes.source: Colonial New England kitchens, Fannie Farmer's Boston Cooking-School Cook Book
recipes.story: Boston Brown Bread was a staple of colonial New England, developed when wheat was scarce and settlers relied on native corn (maize) and imported rye. Traditionally steamed in special cylindrical molds on Saturday and served with baked beans for Sunday dinner (as cooking on the Sabbath was prohibited). The three types of flour represent the agricultural diversity of colonial America.
instructions: Mix all dry ingredients in a large bowl.
Stir in molasses and sour milk.
Pour into greased pudding molds or coffee cans, filling 2/3 full.
Cover tightly with lids or cloth.
Steam for 3 hours in a large pot with water halfway up the molds.
Slice and serve warm with butter.

recipes.title: Shaker Lemon Pie
recipes.description: Slice two lemons as thin as paper, rind and all. Place in a bowl with two cups sugar, mix well and let stand over night or for 24 hours. Then add four well beaten eggs. Pour into a crust-lined pie plate, arrange lemon slices evenly. Cover with top crust, cut several slits near center. Bake in hot oven 15 minutes, reduce heat and bake 30 minutes more or until silver knife inserted comes out clean.
recipes.source: Shaker community records, North Union Shaker Village
recipes.story: This ingenious recipe from the Ohio Shaker community (circa 1800s) demonstrates the sect's commitment to simplicity and waste reduction—the entire lemon, rind and all, is used. The Shakers were known for their innovative agricultural and culinary practices. This pie became a symbol of American resourcefulness and Shaker perfectionism, where economy met elegance.
instructions: Combine lemon slices with sugar in a bowl.
Add beaten eggs and salt to lemon mixture.
Line pie pan with bottom crust.
Pour filling into crust, spreading evenly.
Cover with top crust, seal edges, and cut vents.
Bake at 450°F for 15 minutes, then at 375°F for 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Johnnycakes
recipes.description: Rhode Island cornmeal pancakes. Native American origin.
recipes.story: Journey cakes became johnnycakes. Rhode Island colonists learned this from Narragansett people.

recipes.title: Succotash
recipes.description: Native American dish of beans and corn. Msickquatash.
recipes.story: From Narragansett word. Pilgrims learned this life-sustaining combination from indigenous peoples.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Butter
recipes.description: Spiced pumpkin spread for bread. Colonial preservation.
recipes.story: Early Americans preserved pumpkin for winter. This buttersread on johnny cakes or bread.
instructions: When thick, pack into sterilized jars.

recipes.title: Apple Pandowdy
recipes.description: Dowdy crust pushed into fruit. New England apple dessert.
recipes.story: The 'dowdy' crust is deliberately broken and pushed into the juices. Thrifty colonial baking.
instructions: Pour molasses over, sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon.
Top with broken pieces of pie crust.
Bake 1 hour, breaking crust partway through.

recipes.title: Hasty Pudding
recipes.description: Quick cornmeal porridge. Colonial comfort food.
recipes.story: Made from cornmeal—cheap, fast, filling. Harvard's Hasty Pudding Club named for this dish.
instructions: Serve hot with butter and cream.

recipes.title: Election Cake
recipes.description: Rich fruit bread for election day celebrations.
recipes.story: Baked for Connecticut election days in 1700s. Women contributed these cakes to voting day festivities.
instructions: Add eggs, then dry and wet alternately.

recipes.title: Switchel
recipes.description: Haymaker's drink. Vinegar refresher for harvest.
recipes.story: Colonial farmers drank this during hay harvest. The vinegar was refreshing and prevented dehydration.

recipes.title: Syllabub
recipes.description: Whipped cream and wine dessert. Colonial elegance.
recipes.story: Fashionable in colonial America, served at balls and parties. Light, alcoholic, sophisticated.
instructions: Whip cream with sugar until soft peaks.

recipes.title: Mincemeat
recipes.description: Preserved meat and fruit mixture. Originally with venison.
recipes.story: Colonial preservation method. The name 'mincemeat' comes from minced meat, now mostly fruit.

recipes.title: Corn Dodgers
recipes.description: Hard corn cakes. Civil War soldier food.
recipes.story: Confederate soldiers ate these—easily made over campfires. Dodge means to shape or form.
instructions: Bake on greased sheet at 400°F for 20 minutes.

recipes.title: Samp and Beans
recipes.description: Native American hominy and bean stew.
recipes.story: Algonquian dish adopted by colonists. Samp is hulled corn. Sustained early settlements.
instructions: Simmer with salt pork 3 hours until tender.

recipes.title: Rye and Injun Bread
recipes.description: Mixed grain bread. New England staple when wheat was scarce.
recipes.story: 'Injun' was colonial slang for Indian corn. This bread reflects grain scarcity and adaptation.
instructions: Dissolve yeast in water, add molasses.

recipes.title: Pone
recipes.description: Cornmeal flatbread. Native American pone, Algonquian origin.
recipes.story: From Algonquian 'apan' meaning baked. Simple cornbread baked or fried.
instructions: Bake at 400°F for 30 minutes until crusty.

recipes.title: Flummery
recipes.description: Molded milk pudding. Colonial dessert from England.
recipes.story: Welsh origin, became American with cornstarch. Elegant molded dessert for special occasions.
instructions: Mix cornstarch with little cold milk.

recipes.title: Persimmon Pudding
recipes.description: Wild persimmon dessert. Native American fruit pudding.
recipes.story: Native Americans introduced colonists to persimmons. This pudding became a Southern tradition.
instructions: Mix persimmon with sugar and eggs.

recipes.title: Hominy Grits
recipes.description: Stone-ground corn porridge. Southern breakfast staple.
recipes.story: From Algonquian 'rockahominy.' Nixtamalized corn ground coarse. Foundation of Southern cuisine.
instructions: Bring water and salt to boil.
Reduce heat, simmer 20-25 minutes, stirring often.

recipes.title: Shrub
recipes.description: Vinegar-preserved fruit syrup. Colonial refreshment.
recipes.story: Pre-refrigeration preservation. The vinegar preserved fruit for mixing with water—colonial soda.
instructions: Strain, add sugar, heat until dissolved.
Mix 1 part shrub to 3 parts sparkling water.

recipes.title: Indian Pudding (Baked)
recipes.description: Slow-baked cornmeal pudding. New England classic.
recipes.story: Different from Adams' stovetop version—this is baked long and slow. Colonial comfort dessert.

recipes.title: Corn Oysters
recipes.description: Fritters shaped like oysters. Mock oysters for inland tables.
recipes.story: When oysters were unavailable, corn fritters provided a similar shape. Clever colonial cooking.
instructions: Mix all ingredients to make thick batter.
Fry until golden on both sides.

recipes.title: Anadama Bread
recipes.description: Anna, damn her! Legend says a fisherman cursed his wife's cornmeal mush.
recipes.story: Massachusetts legend: a fisherman tired of cornmeal mush added flour and yeast, cursing 'Anna, damn her!' Hence the name.
instructions: Stir cornmeal into boiling water, cook until thick.
Add molasses, butter, salt. Cool to lukewarm.
Add to cornmeal mixture with flour.

recipes.title: Sally Lunn Bread
recipes.description: Rich egg bread. English immigrant recipe.
recipes.story: Named for Sally Lunn who sold these in Bath, England. Became American colonial favorite—rich, cake-like bread.
instructions: Let rise 1 hour in greased bundt pan.

recipes.title: Ash Cakes
recipes.description: Cornbread baked in fireplace ashes. Frontier simplicity.
recipes.story: When settlers had no pots or ovens, they baked in ashes. Most basic bread possible.
instructions: Mix cornmeal, salt, and enough water to form stiff dough.
Wrap in cabbage leaves or corn husks.

recipes.title: Spider Corn Cake
recipes.description: Cake baked in a 'spider'—cast iron pan with legs for hanging over coals.
recipes.story: The spider was a legged skillet used in hearth cooking. This creates a custard layer when milk is added on top.
instructions: Beat in sour milk, eggs, molasses.
Melt butter in cast iron spider (pan with legs).
Pour sweet milk over top (don't stir).
Bake at 425°F for 30 minutes until set.
